title: B-CELL IMMUNODEFICIENCY, DISTAL LIMB ANOMALIES, AND UROGENITAL MALFORMATIONS

relationships.phenotype: B-CELL IMMUNODEFICIENCY, DISTAL LIMB ANOMALIES, AND UROGENITAL MALFORMATIONS

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that B-cell immunodeficiency, distal limb anomalies, and urogenital malformations (BILU), also known as Hoffman syndrome, is caused by heterozygous mutation in the TOP2B gene (126431) on chromosome 3p24.2.

checks.claim: B-cell immunodeficiency, distal limb anomalies, and urogenital malformations (BILU), also known as Hoffman syndrome, is caused by heterozygous mutation in the TOP2B gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Here, we show that mutations in TOP2B underlie the syndromic B-cell immunodeficiency
checks.explanation: Paper shows heterozygous TOP2B mutations cause the syndromic B-cell immunodeficiency named Hoffman syndrome; the BILU name and urogenital features are OMIM nomenclature not stated in the paper.

checks.claim: The TOP2B gene is located on chromosome 3p24.2.
checks.evidence_quote: One gene, TOP2B, which encodes topoisomerase IIβ, was affected by a heterozygous variant in each family
checks.explanation: Chromosomal location is standard nomenclature not stated in the paper; accepted as restating gene identity.

paragraphs.text: Hoffman syndrome is an autosomal dominant disorder (Tischkowitz et al., 2004). It consists of humoral immunodeficiency with low or absent B cells (Hoffman et al., 2001; Hügle et al., 2011) and hypogammaglobulinemia, which leads to recurrent infections (Hoffman et al., 2001). It also involves distal limb anomalies, such as syndactyly and other digit malformations (Hoffman et al., 2001), and malformations of the urogenital tract (Edery et al., 2001). Facial dysmorphism has also been described (Hoffman et al., 2001).

checks.claim: Hoffman syndrome is an autosomal dominant disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: Here, we report a second family with similar features, which also shows autosomal dominant inheritance.
checks.explanation: The paper (title and abstract) describes the B-cell immunodeficiency, limb anomaly and urogenital malformation syndrome (BILU) as autosomal dominant.

checks.claim: Hoffman syndrome includes humoral immunodeficiency with low or absent B cells.
checks.evidence_quote: Laboratory evaluation revealed hypogammaglobulinaemia, absent B cells, and a 46,XX karyotype.
checks.explanation: The paper reports a humoral immune deficiency with absent B cells. That fits the draft's 'low or absent' wording; 'low' probably comes from the other paper the draft cites.

checks.claim: Hoffman syndrome includes hypogammaglobulinemia, which leads to recurrent infections.
checks.evidence_quote: Her clinical course has been complicated by recurrent sinopulmonary infections and pneumococcal bacteraemia. Laboratory evaluation revealed hypogammaglobulinaemia
checks.explanation: The paper reports both hypogammaglobulinemia and recurrent infections. The causal link isn't stated but is clearly implied.

checks.claim: Hoffman syndrome includes distal limb anomalies such as syndactyly and other digit malformations.
checks.evidence_quote: thenar hypoplasia, partial 4-5 syndactyly of toes, recessed great toes, anterior anus, and hypoplastic labia minora. Radiographic findings include triphalangeal thumbs and hypoplastic first metatarsals.
checks.explanation: The paper reports syndactyly and other malformations of the fingers and toes.

checks.claim: Hoffman syndrome includes malformations of the urogenital tract.
checks.evidence_quote: B cell immunodeficiency, distal limb abnormalities, and urogenital malformations in a three generation family: a novel autosomal dominant syndrome?
checks.explanation: Only the title was supplied. It lists urogenital malformations as part of a syndrome with B cell immunodeficiency and distal limb abnormalities. However, it presents this as a possibly new autosomal dominant syndrome and never names it Hoffman syndrome or links it to that condition. That link isn't supported by the supplied text.

checks.claim: Facial dysmorphism has been described in Hoffman syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Physical findings include microcephaly, micrognathia, sickle shaped eyebrows, hypoplastic alae nasi
checks.explanation: The paper describes facial dysmorphism; its title also refers to facial dysmorphology.

paragraphs.text: Papapietro et al. (2020) concluded that BILU and Hoffman syndromes are manifestations of the same disease, TOP2B deficiency.

checks.claim: Papapietro et al. (2020) concluded that BILU and Hoffman syndromes are manifestations of the same disease, TOP2B deficiency.
checks.evidence_quote: Our results indicate that BILU and Hoffman syndromes are manifestations of the same disease, TOP2B deficiency.
checks.explanation: The paper states this conclusion directly.

paragraphs.text: Hoffman et al. (2001) reported a 6-year-old girl with an isolated humoral immune deficiency and a unique combination of dysmorphic features. Laboratory evaluation showed hypogammaglobulinemia and absent B cells, and she had recurrent sinopulmonary infections and pneumococcal bacteremia. She had distal limb anomalies, with triphalangeal thumbs and hypoplastic first metatarsals on radiographs, and also had hypoplastic labia minora and an anterior anus.

paragraphs.text: Hügle et al. (2011) noted that this sporadic case of humoral immunodeficiency, facial dysmorphism, and limb anomalies in a young girl was later referred to as Hoffman syndrome.

checks.claim: Hügle et al. (2011) noted that the sporadic case of humoral immunodeficiency, facial dysmorphism, and limb anomalies in a young girl was later referred to as Hoffman syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: One such report was a sporadic case of humoral immunodeficiency, facial dysmorphism, and limb anomalies in a young girl, later referred to as Hoffman syndrome.

paragraphs.text: Hoffman et al. (2001) suggested that the patient they reported might represent a unique syndrome of unknown etiology. Tischkowitz et al. (2004) reported a second family with similar features showing autosomal dominant inheritance. Broderick et al. (2019) found autosomal dominant mutations in the TOP2B gene, confirming autosomal dominant inheritance.

checks.claim: Hoffman et al. (2001) suggested that the patient they reported might represent a unique syndrome of unknown etiology.
checks.evidence_quote: She may represent a unique syndrome of unknown etiology.
checks.explanation: The abstract says this directly about the reported patient.

checks.claim: Tischkowitz et al. (2004) reported a second family with features similar to the patient reported by Hoffman et al. (2001).
checks.evidence_quote: A family with an unusual combination of B-cell immunodeficiency, distal limb abnormalities, genitourinary malformations, and mild dysmorphic features has recently been described. Here, we report a second family with similar features
checks.explanation: The abstract reports a second family with features similar to a recently described first family. The abstract does not name Hoffman et al. (2001) and calls the earlier report a family rather than a single patient, but the draft's framing fits this.

checks.claim: The family reported by Tischkowitz et al. (2004) showed autosomal dominant inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: Here, we report a second family with similar features, which also shows autosomal dominant inheritance.

checks.claim: Broderick et al. (2019) found autosomal dominant mutations in the TOP2B gene in this syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Sequencing of patients with B cell-restricted immunodeficiency reveals autosomal dominant mutations in TOP2B.
checks.explanation: The abstract says outright that autosomal dominant TOP2B mutations were found in patients with this syndrome, which the paper calls Hoffman syndrome.

checks.claim: The finding of autosomal dominant TOP2B mutations by Broderick et al. (2019) confirmed autosomal dominant inheritance of this syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: We previously described two unrelated families with autosomal dominant inherited syndromic B-cell immunodeficiency of unknown etiology,. While agammaglobulinemia and hypogammaglobulinemia are common to several classic immunodeficiencies, the patients were also affected by facial dysmorphism, and limb anomalies
checks.explanation: The paper describes the families as having an autosomal dominant inherited disorder and reports heterozygous TOP2B mutations in all three families. Those mutations act dominantly in yeast and in mice, so they fit autosomal dominant inheritance. The paper never uses the word 'confirming', but that conclusion follows directly from what it reports.

paragraphs.text: Broderick et al. (2019) studied 2 previously reported unrelated families with autosomal dominant syndromic B-cell immunodeficiency of unknown etiology and a third patient first described as having atypical Ablepharon-Macrostomia syndrome. Filtering variants within each family on the assumption of a dominant inheritance pattern, they identified 3 heterozygous mutations in the TOP2B gene affecting the TOPRIM, or DNA gating, domain of topoisomerase II-beta. Two of the mutations were missense, and one was a de novo in-frame deletion. Functional studies showed that the patient mutations had a dominant-negative effect on enzyme function. In mouse models, the mutations caused a block in B-cell development.

checks.evidence_quote: We previously reported two unrelated families with autosomal dominant inherited syndromic B-cell immunodeficiency of unknown etiology

checks.evidence_quote: We filtered variants within each family assuming that the variants would not be in dbSNP, would have a dominant inheritance pattern, and would affect coding sequences

checks.evidence_quote: we identified three heterozygous mutations affecting the TOPRIM, or DNA gating, domain of the type II topoisomerase TOP2B.

checks.claim: The 3 TOP2B mutations identified by Broderick et al. (2019) affect the TOPRIM, or DNA gating, domain of topoisomerase II-beta.
checks.evidence_quote: we identified three heterozygous mutations affecting the TOPRIM, or DNA gating, domain of the type II topoisomerase TOP2B.

checks.claim: Two of the 3 TOP2B mutations identified by Broderick et al. (2019) were missense mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: Three variants were identified: a missense mutation c.1448C > T, p.S483L, a de novo inframe deletion c.1761_1763AGAdel p.EE587E, a missense mutation c.1897G > A, p. G633S.

checks.claim: One of the 3 TOP2B mutations identified by Broderick et al. (2019) was an in-frame deletion.
checks.evidence_quote: a de novo in-frame deletion c.1761_1763delAGA, p.EE587E, and a missense mutation c.1448C > T, p.S483L

checks.claim: The TOP2B in-frame deletion identified by Broderick et al. (2019) occurred de novo.
checks.evidence_quote: a de novo in-frame deletion c.1761_1763delAGA, p.EE587E

checks.claim: Functional studies by Broderick et al. (2019) showed that the patient TOP2B mutations had a dominant-negative effect on enzyme function.
checks.evidence_quote: demonstrate that patient mutations in TOP2B have a dominant negative effect on enzyme function
checks.explanation: Stated in abstract; yeast data describe a partial dominant negative effect.

checks.claim: In mouse models by Broderick et al. (2019), the patient TOP2B mutations caused a block in B-cell development.
checks.evidence_quote: resulting in defective proliferation, survival of B-2 cells, causing a block in B cell development, and impair humoral function in response to immunization
checks.explanation: Stated in abstract; knockin mouse modeled EE587E.

paragraphs.text: Papapietro et al. (2020) independently reported a heterozygous TOP2B mutation in patients with B-cell deficiency and syndromic features.

checks.claim: Papapietro et al. (2020) independently reported a heterozygous TOP2B mutation in patients with B-cell deficiency and syndromic features.
checks.evidence_quote: This heterozygous G>C mutation at the cDNA nucleotide 1,453 of the TOP2B gene (ENST00000435706) resulted in the alanine to proline substitution at position 485 (A485P) of topoisomerase 2β (TOP2B).
checks.explanation: The paper reports a heterozygous TOP2B mutation in BILU patients, who have B-cell deficiency together with limb and urogenital anomalies.
